restrictions: Two-block ordinary collision under the standard IV: SHA-256 compression, first 40 steps, standard padding and feed-forward, all 256 output bits equal; block 1 differs (M0 != M0') and block 2 differs (N != N'), the common padding block preserving the collision. v5 primitives only, no ctz/clz/popcount; one 40-step target compression = 1 unit, every other primitive word operation = 1/C.

Block-1 cost carries the accepted board-best R40 walk df1f1cd1 (123.90702 at the 0.61 success floor, lambda0 = -ln 0.61) as its per-eval anchor; the 254-bit map psi = (a..g, h mod 2^30) reduction (-1/2 log2 3 = -0.79248) rests on premise P1, the df1f1cd1 random-function premise applied to psi. Usable-outcome law: dh uniform on {0, 2^30, 2^31, 3*2^30}, three of four usable.

Block-2 cost carries the best accepted r39 base (9993eaa8 / 9993eaa8, 116.58624) and the 5f8e6192 term decomposition (claw +9.8077, W17 pin +32.0000, tail +74.3238, ops/claw +1.5647, leader tightening -0.0609); premise H1 (claw rates and W17 pin) is declared to transfer to constants K1..K39 since the constants change value conditions only, never differences. Rows <= 16 executed: r39_K16, 3/3 SAT, 0 violations.

Premise H2 (tail, -log2 p >= 74.3238) transfer to K1..K39 is supported by the shifted-constant histogram comparison over 2^30 samples per junction (tailshift.sh, J22 443,739,873 vs 443,737,969 kept, 4,187 vs 4,251 at weight 6).

Shared work budget: one driver (price40d.py) runs the 254-bit walk until the first usable collision, then block 2 in the remaining budget W. Walk P(T1<=t)=1-exp(-lambda0 (t/2^a0)^2), a0=123.11454; block 2 1-exp(-lambda0 (W-T1)/2^b0), b0=116.5437. Success(W)=E[1{T1<=W}(1/3+2/3 P2(W-T1))]=0.39, giving log2 W = 123.13485.

Memory: both blocks run sequentially on one shared 2^20-byte distinguished-point arena (peak 1,047,428 B < 1,048,576), so memory_log2_bytes = 20 and the memory term max(0, 19.998-20) = 0; block-2 advice preprocessing (2^36) adds nothing to the time ledger.
